name: YouTube upload from a Telegram folder path (private)

parameters.content:
## 1 · Path from Telegram → folder check
Send the bot the path of a folder (Explorer: Ctrl+Shift+C → paste). No n8n server runs in between: the desktop shortcut runs `scripts/telegram_check.py`, which fetches new messages and starts this workflow once per message (`n8n execute`, message in `TG_MESSAGE`); n8n exits when the run is done. Only the chat in `TELEGRAM_CHAT_ID` is accepted. `scripts/intake.py` finds the video, the optional text file (Title / Description / Tags) and up to two thumbnails, and links them into `work/`. The path reaches the shell only hex-encoded.

## 2 · Linked video, fill in what is missing
Shorts link the channel's latest public video longer than 3 minutes at the top of the description (or the video named after the path / in `Related:`; `no link` skips it). Three read-only YouTube API calls (channels → uploads playlist → videos); a failed lookup only skips the link. The Shorts 'Related video' field itself has no API, the reply says what to pick in Studio.

Fields from the text file are used as written. Only if title, description or tags are missing: faster-whisper transcribes the video and the local LLM (Ollama) writes the missing fields with the channel's preset prompt and style guide.

## 3 · Upload, set visibility, reply, log
Upload to YouTube as **private**, set thumbnail A, then switch to the wanted visibility (word after the path in the message, `Privacy:` in the text file, or `DEFAULT_PRIVACY`), so a public video never shows without its thumbnail. A date and time (`18.11. 18:00`) schedules it instead: private until then, then public (YouTube's publishAt). The YouTube API takes one thumbnail per video, so B is for A/B testing in YouTube Studio (long videos only; Shorts have no thumbnail test). Reply in Telegram with links, append a line to `logs/runs.csv`.

parameters.text: =📂 Send me the path of a folder. In Explorer: select the folder, press Ctrl+Shift+C (copy as path), paste it here. The folder holds: • one video (mp4, mov, mkv, webm, m4v) • optional meta.txt with Title:, Tags:, Description:. Whatever is missing, the local LLM writes. • up to two thumbnails (jpg, png): A = first by file name, B = second Visibility: private unless you add public or unlisted after the path, or a Privacy: line in meta.txt. Schedule: add a date and time after the path, e.g. 18.11. 18:00 or morgen 18 Uhr (PC clock), or a Publish: line in meta.txt. It stays private until then and goes public by itself.

messageValues.message:
You write YouTube metadata for one channel. You get the channel's style guide and a timestamped transcript of the video.

Rules:
- Write title, description, tags and thumbnail_text in the metadata language given in the request, even if the video is spoken in another language.
- Title: at most 70 characters, specific and concrete, the most searchable words first. No clickbait, no ALL CAPS, no emojis, no hashtags.
- Description: 2 to 4 short paragraphs. The first sentence says what the viewer gets and works on its own in search results. Only state what is in the transcript; never invent facts, names, numbers or promises. No hashtags and no links (the channel footer is added later).
- tags: 8 to 15 search phrases a viewer would type, specific to this video, lower case, no hashtags, no duplicates of each other.
- thumbnail_text: 2 to 5 words in the metadata language that make someone click, no punctuation except ? or !.
- chapters: only for videos longer than 3 minutes: at least 3 entries, the first at 0:00, times as m:ss taken from the transcript, short titles. For shorter videos return an empty list.
- Follow the channel style guide below where it is more specific than these rules.
- If the request contains extra instructions from the uploader, follow them for the title, wording, focus and tone. They take priority over the channel style guide, but never over the rule against inventing facts.
- The request lists the fields the uploader already wrote. Return those unchanged and write only the fields marked MISSING, so that they fit what the uploader wrote.
- Answer with the JSON object only.

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ id: $('Upload to YouTube (private)').first().json.uploadId, status: { privacyStatus: $('Final metadata').first().json.publishAt ? 'private' : $('Final metadata').first().json.privacy, publishAt: $('Final metadata').first().json.publishAt || undefined, embeddable: true, license: 'youtube', publicStatsViewable: true, selfDeclaredMadeForKids: $('Final metadata').first().json.madeForKids } }) }}
